In this appeal, filed under Section 23 of the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 (for short, 'the Act of 1987'), the challenge is to the judgment and order dated 01.03.2018, passed by the Railway Claims Tribunal, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur (for short 'the Tribunal'), whereby the claim filed by the appellants/claimants for compensation under Section 16 of the Act of 1987 was dismissed.

Background facts:
Appellant No. 1 is the wife of the deceased - Puran Gautela.
Appellant Nos. 2 to 4 are the sons of the deceased.
They claim that on 01.01.2015, after purchasing a journey ticket, the deceased boarded a train at Nagpur to go to Badnera.
The ticket was purchased for the deceased by appellant No. 2.
The deceased boarded the train with a valid journey ticket.

They stated that due to a heavy rush in the train and a sudden jerk to the train,
the deceased fell from the running train and sustained serious injuries between pole No.

He was shifted to Indira Gandhi Government Medical College for treatment by the railway police.
His one leg was amputated in the accident.
He died on 02.01.2015, due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
According to the appellants, the deceased was a bona fide passenger travelling with a valid journey ticket.
He died in an untoward incident.
Therefore, they claimed the compensation.
4 Respondent-railway filed the written statement and opposed the claim.
It is the contention of the railway that the death was not in an untoward incident.
The deceased was not a bona fide passenger.
The possibility of the deceased being run over by any train or dashed by the train at the spot of the incident can't be ruled out.
5 Appellant No.2 examined himself as a sole witness in support of the claim.
The railway did not adduce oral evidence.
Learned Members of the Tribunal, on consideration 902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt of the evidence, found that there was no substance in the claim and ultimately, dismissed the claim.

7 In the facts and circumstances,
the following points fall for my determination:
(i) Whether the deceased died in an untoward incident as understood by the provisions of Section 123(c)(2) of the Railways Act, 1989?

Learned Advocate submitted that in such an accident, the possibility of loss of a ticket can't be ruled out.
Learned Advocate submitted that the possibility of loss of the ticket has been established.
Learned Advocate submitted that, therefore, the finding recorded by the Tribunal, on this point, can't be sustained.

Learned Advocate submitted that the spot of the incident is at some distance from the Nagpur Railway Station platform.

Learned Advocate submitted that the train, after departing from the platform,
moves in a slow speed and therefore, the possibility of the passenger getting crushed under the wheel of the train can't be ruled out.
Learned Advocate submitted that the case is covered by the provisions of Section 124-A of the Railways Act, 1989 and therefore, the learned Members were not right in rejecting this contention.

11 The question with regard to the burden of proof and standard of evidence to prove the factum of the journey with a valid railway ticket has been dealt with by the Hon'ble Apex Court, in the case of Union of India .v/s. Rina Devi 1.
In this context, before perusal of the cross examination and other evidence adduced by the appellants, it would be apt to make a useful reference to Para No.29 of the above decision.
It is extracted below:

"29. We thus hold that mere presence of a body on the Railway premises will not be conclusive to hold that the injured or deceased was a bona fide passenger for which a claim for compensation could be maintained.
However, mere absence of a ticket with such an injured or deceased person will not negative the claim that he was a bona fide passenger.
The initial burden will be on the 1 (2019) 3 SCC 572 902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt claimant, which can be discharged by filing an affidavit of the relevant facts.
and burden will then shift on the Railways and the issue can be decided on the facts shown or the attending circumstances.
This will have to be dealt with from case to case on the basis of facts found.
The legal position in this regard will stand explained accordingly."

12 The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that mere presence of body on the railway premises will not be conclusive to hold that the injured or deceased was a bona fide passenger for which claim for compensation could be maintained.
It is further held that mere absence of ticket with such injured or deceased will not negative the claim that he was a bona fide passenger.

It is held that the initial burden will be on the claimant, which can be discharged by filing an affidavit of relevant facts and the burden will then shift on the railways, and the issue can be decided on the basis of the facts shown or the attending circumstances.
It is held that this will have to be dealt with from case to case on the basis of the facts found.

14 The statement of AW-1 was recorded by railway police on 19.01.2015.
The statement is at Exh.A-5.
In this statement, he categorically stated that on the date of the incident, he accompanied his father to the railway station and purchased the ticket for his father to go to Badnera.
He has stated that after dropping his father, he went back.
On perusal of the statutory report as well as the DRM report, it is evident that both documents are silent about this aspect.
The police as well as the DRM were expected to record a finding, on the basis of the material collected during the course of investigation, that this statement made by AW-1 was not correct.
So this is one circumstance that supports the contention of the appellants and ultimately, the contention of the AW-1 on this aspect.
902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt 15
There is one more circumstance to accept the contention of the appellants with regard to the loss of the journey ticket, as contended by them.
The deceased was found in an injured condition at the spot of the incident.
The possibility of loss of a ticket in such an incident can't be ruled out.
It is not the case of the railway that the spot of the incident was inspected by the railway officials immediately after the incident.

It has come on the record that on the basis of the report of the railway officials, the police went to the spot and immediately shifted the deceased to the Government Hospital, in an injured condition.
The spot of the incident was neither guarded by the police nor by the railway administration.

Learned Members of the Tribunal, on the basis of the facts recorded in the spot panchanama and the inquest panchanama, have concluded that at the time of the drawing of both panchanamas, the ticket was not found.
In my view, learned Members have failed to consider the above stated facts 902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt as well as the delay on the part of the police to draw the spot panchanama.
The incident, admittedly, occurred on 01.01.2015.
The spot panchanama was drawn on 05.01.2015.
It is not the case of the railway that before drawing the panchanama immediately after the incident, the spot was inspected.
If the ticket had been lost on the spot, by no stretch of imagination, it could be said that it would be traced out after five days of the incident.
Therefore, on the basis of the facts recorded in the panchanama and the findings recorded on the basis of the same cannot be sustained.

The deceased succumbed to the injuries on 02.01.2015.

In the facts and circumstances, there ought to have been a positive evidence to rule out the possibility of loss of a ticket in this process.
In my view, the evidence of AW-1 is required to be appreciated, keeping all these facts in mind.
The evidence on record is sufficient to discharge the initial burden.
On the basis of this evidence, the appellants have proved that the deceased was a bona fide passenger travelling with a valid journey ticket.
The case of the appellants, in my view, is squarely covered by the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rina 902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt Devi (supra).
The evidence can't be discarded.
There is no evidence in rebuttal.
As such, the findings recorded by the learned Members of the Tribunal on this point cannot be sustained.
17 The next important point is whether the deceased died in an untoward incident or not.
There is hardly any dispute about the occurrence of the incident.
I have already observed that the railway has not adduced the evidence to prove that the deceased was run over or dashed by any train at the spot of the incident.
It is the case of the respondent-railway that the house of the deceased was adjacent to the railway track and therefore, while moving on the track he might have been run over by any train.
It needs to be stated that on the basis of the amputation of one leg an inference of run over of the deceased by any train cannot be drawn.
There is no report of the loco-pilot or guard of any train about dash to any person or run over of any person at the spot of the incident.
The incident 902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt occurred during daytime.

If the deceased was run over or dashed by any train, at the spot of incident, then the loco-pilot as well as the guard of said train would have reported such an incident to the station master at Nagpur railway station.
In my view, this is a very important circumstance in favour of the appellants and against the respondent.
18 The evidence of AW-1 that he accompanied the deceased to the railway station and purchased a railway ticket for the deceased has been found to be worth credible and acceptable.
He has stated that the deceased after collecting the ticket from him went to the platform to board the train to go to Badnera.
On the basis of his evidence, the appellants have proved that the deceased had entered the railway station with a valid journey ticket to go to Badnera.
The spot of the incident is not at the railway station.
It is at some distance from the railway platform towards Badnera side.
It is common knowledge that after departure, the train moves slowly.
The 902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt spot of the incident is not far away from the Badnera end of the platform of Nagpur railway station.
The possibility of a person coming under the wheels by a fall from a slow moving train can't be ruled out.
There is no eye witness to the incident.
Simply because of the amputation of the leg of the deceased an inference cannot be drawn that he was run over at the spot of the incident by any train.
19 As per Section 123(c)(2) of the Railway Act, 1989, the accidental falling of a passenger from a moving train carrying passengers is an untoward incident.
The compensation cannot be denied to the injured or to the dependents of the deceased on the specious plea of negligence or contributory Smt.

Under Section 124-A of the Railways Act, 1989, the liability to pay compensation is regardless of any wrongful act, neglect or default on the part of the railway administration.
The railway administration cannot be held liable to pay the compensation, in case the death of the 902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt
passenger
or injury to the passenger is caused due to any of the reasons enumerated in clauses (a) to (e) to proviso to Section 124-A.

In my view,
on this point, the decision in the case of Rina Devi (supra) would also be helpful.
Para No. 25 is relevant for this purpose.
It is extracted below:

"25. We are unable to uphold the above view as the concept of 'self inflicted injury'
would require intention to inflict such injury and not mere negligence of any particular degree.
Doing so would amount to invoking the principle of contributory negligence which cannot be done in the case of liability based on 'no fault theory'.

We may in this connection refer to judgment of this Court in United India Insurance Co.
Ltd. versus Sunil Kumar laying down that plea of negligence of the victim cannot be allowed in claim based on 'no fault theory' under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

sentences.text: Accordingly, we hold that death or injury in the course of boarding or de- boarding a train will be an 'untoward incident' entitling a victim to the compensation and will not fall under the proviso to Section 124-A merely on the plea of negligence of the victim as a contributing factor."
902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt 20
The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that for the purpose of accepting the case of self inflicted injury, there must be intention to inflict the injury and not mere negligence of any particular degree.
In such a case the defence of negligence or contributory negligence cannot be invoked.
It is held that the liability in the claim is based on the principle of strict liability or no fault theory.

It is further held that the death or injury in the course of boarding and de-boarding a train will be an 'untoward incident' entitling a victim to the compensation and will not fall under the proviso to Section 124A merely on the plea of negligence of the victim as a contributing factor.
21 In the present case, the possibility of the deceased, being run over at the spot of the incident has been completely ruled out.
There is no iota of evidence on record to accept the contention of the respondent-railway on this point.

The evidence of AW1 is sufficient to prove that the deceased boarded some unknown train at Nagpur Railway Station to go 902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt to Badnera and on the way fell from a moving train at the spot of the incident and ultimately, died.
22 It is further pertinent to mention that AW-1 could have improved his case and stated that he had seen the deceased boarding some train at Nagpur Railway Station, but he did not do so.
It is evident that he has narrated the facts to which he was privy.
In my view, therefore, there is no reason to discard and disbelieve the evidence that the deceased was found injured on the railway premises.
The learned Members of the Tribunal, in my view, have failed to properly appreciate the evidence and provisions of law as discussed above and came to a wrong conclusion.

Therefore, on both points,
the finding recorded by the Tribunal cannot be sustained.
As such, I record my findings on both points in the affirmative.
In view of this appeal deserves to be allowed.

Learned Advocate for the respondent submitted that after issuance of notification dated 22.12.2016 by the Ministry of Railways (Railway Board), the compensation payable under the various entries of Schedule to the Railway Accidents and Untoward Incidents (Compensation) Rules, 1990 has been revised with effect from 01.01.2017.
In view of the amendment of the schedule, in case of a death claim, the claimants are entitled to get compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-.
However, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the Case of Union of India .v/s. Radha Yadav 2 in the case of the old claim, the appellants/claimants would be entitled to get compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- without interest.
Therefore, in this case, the claimants would be entitled to get Rs.8,00,000/- without interest.
24 Accordingly, I pass the following order:
(i) The first appeal is allowed.
2 (2019) 3 SCC 410 902.FA.888.2019 railway compensation judge.odt
(ii) The judgment and order dated 01.03.2018 passed by the Railway Claims Tribunal, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur in Claim Application No. OA(IIu)/NGP/2015/ 0059 is quashed and set aside.
The claim application is allowed.
(iii) The respondent-railway is directed to pay Rs.8,00,000/-(Rupees Eight Lacs Only) towards compensation to the appellants/claimants.
(iv) Appellant No. 1 shall be paid 55 % of the amount of compensation.
(v) Appellant Nos. 2 to 4 shall be paid 15 % of the amount of compensation each.
(vi) The compensation amount of Rs.8,00,000/-
be deposited with the Registry of this Court within four months.
If the amount is not deposited within four months, the amount shall carry interest @ of 7% p.a. from the date of this order until realization of the amount.
After depositing the balance amount, the appellants are permitted to withdraw the amount,
with accrued interest, if any.
The first appeal stands disposed of.
Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
